verdict.label: weak generalisation — keep but de-claim
verdict.reason: On 6-element disjoint holdout: useful_rate A=B=100% (TIE); composite A=1.056 vs B=1.028 (A better by +0.028, only just above 2pp threshold). The cycle-4 +17pp / +0.183 numbers DID NOT reproduce — both sides hit the 100% ceiling on this slice, so the cycle's incumbent of 83% useful was slice-bias-low. The only real signal is +5pp SMT feasibility (61% vs 56%).

notes: Honest take: the cycle-4 '+17pp useful, +0.183 composite' headline was inflated by an unfortunate eval-slice draw where the incumbent underperformed at 83%. On the held-out slice the baseline already reaches 100%, so the winner has nowhere to push useful_rate. The CONCRETE ARTIFACTS directive is not harmful and gives ~+5pp SMT feasibility, so retention is justified — but README/baseline metrics should NOT be updated upward from cycle 4 alone. Next cycle should target SMT feasibility or family-bias rather than useful_rate, where headroom remains.

verdict.label: B WORSE — REVERTED
verdict.reason: At N=30 (29 overlap, same seed/sources as prior REBASELINE): useful 97%->87% (-10pp), caught 33%->20% (-13pp), missed 3%->13% (+10pp, 4x worse), SMT 82%->82% (n=6 +5pp was noise), family share 47%->67% (+20pp worse bias). Composite 1.144->0.944. 7 net per-element regressions; only 1 partial->caught transition.

notes: The CONCRETE ARTIFACTS directive forces concrete file/symbol references in steps. On danluu post-mortems and operational-rollout cases that need high-level stakeholder coordination this produces worse plans. The cycle-4 +17pp gain on n=6 eval slice was eval-slice bias (incumbent unluckily underperformed at 83%); the n=6 holdout's 'weak generalisation' verdict (+0.028 composite) was underpowered noise. N=30 is the right granularity to gate prompt changes. Lesson: GEPA cycles must validate at N=30 (or at least N=20) before claiming a win, not n=6 where ceiling effects + variance dominate. Updated gepa_optimizer's default --holdout-n recommendation to 20 in the calibration record (no code change until next cycle so existing flags don't break).

verdict.label: TENTATIVE — APPLIED for family-balance reason
verdict.reason: Same n=48 seed-1337 elements compared --prefer balanced (A) vs --prefer safe (B). max-family-share 67% -> 58% (-8pp) + robust_launch unblocked from 0 to 2 wins. judge caught_rate 38% -> 40% (+2pp); literal caught_rate 52% -> 56% (+4pp). Both caught-rate deltas inside n=48 sample noise (~±20pp at α=0.05) — not statistically significant. Family-share -8pp is borderline-significant and matches the intended fix direction. Applied for family-balance reason; do NOT claim caught-rate improvement until validated at higher N or on a held-out slice.

notes: Per-element transitions: 9 partial->caught, 8 caught->partial, 10 caught->caught, 21 partial->partial. Net +1 caught — basically a wash on individual elements. The directional family-balance win (-8pp max-share, +2 robust_launch wins) is the real signal. launch_strategy_ok unchanged at 71%/71% — confirms weight tuning does NOT fix the launch-strategy mismatch (29% wrong-strategy in baseline). That requires gepa_revise on the sequencer prompt, not weight rebalancing. Next cycle target. Cycle-4 lesson encoded: don't claim caught-rate gains from single-slice n<100 A/B; only accept directional family-share or explicit held-out validation.
